name: Lib-INVENT with docking and RFXscore
one_liner: A scaffold-decorating molecule generator is rewarded with Glide docking and a trained rescoring model, and its weights are updated toward high scorers.

loop.proposes: Decorations (substituents) added to a factor Xa scaffold, written as SMILES by Lib-INVENT, a REINVENT variant
loop.judged_by: Glide XP docking, ligand efficiency, the RFXscore rescoring model, QED and a factor Xa QSAR model
loop.steers: Reinforcement learning updates the generator's agent network; a diversity filter penalises repeats

headline_result: In a factor Xa case study, docking followed by RFXscore gave the best results, especially when diverse structures fitting a binding site were wanted; RFXscore plus the factor Xa model left the most compounds after MM/GBSA and other filters. RFXscore had a test r2 of 0.494 and MAE of 1.086.
caveat: MM/GBSA was applied afterwards as an independent check, not as a training reward. Everything is computed binding, with no lab measurements, and the target is a single well-studied protein (factor Xa).
beyond_harness_note: A SMILES generator is trained by a reward built from docking and a learned rescoring model rather than being prompted.
generative_model: Lib-INVENT RNN prior and agent (scaffold decoration)
algorithmic_authority: Glide XP docking, RFXscore rescoring, MM/GBSA post-check

sources.title: Optimizing interactions to protein binding sites by integrating docking-scoring strategies into generative AI methods (Frontiers in Chemistry 2022)

verification.notes: Opened the Frontiers full text (first 100,000 characters). Authors Sauer, Matter, Hessler, Grebner (Sanofi), published 19 Oct 2022. Confirmed: Glide XP and ligand efficiency, RFXscore, QED and fXa QSAR used as rewards; MM/GBSA (OPLS3e, threshold -70 kcal/mol) and MedChem filters applied afterwards, matching the draft's note that MM/GBSA is not in every step (it is never a training reward). The draft's 'Glide docking + scoring in the reward' is correct. Parent set to reinvent-4 per instruction, though Lib-INVENT originates in a 2021 paper not opened here.
